title: He Slept For Ten Years, Then Ran Until He Collapsed . . . (Part 1)
caption:
Airen Farreira slept for ten years, then picked up a sword in The Lazy Lord Masters the Sword.
The lazy lord enters a sword academy and trains until his body breaks. Follow for part 2!

#thelazylordmasterstheSword #manhwarecap #manhwa #webtoon #fyp
credit: The Lazy Lord Masters the Sword (Dodomoon / Doip / Second Star)
comment: Would you quit the run like everyone expected, or get up like Airen? Why? 👀 Comment below 👇

segments.say: The Lazy Lord just ran until his legs quit, and now four hundred *recruits* watch him collapse.
To see how it got here, go back to a *dream* about a stranger and his sword.
A stranger walks into a tiny village, says nothing, and *swings* a sword every single day.
The villagers gossip, but the old man writing this diary couldn't care *less*.
Years pass. He marries a girl named Rema, and they have a daughter, *Laura*.
Thirty-seven years later the gate is rotting and the village has changed, but the stranger *hasn't*.
One morning the old man pushes the gate open and *freezes*.
The stranger died on his knees with his sword in his hands, so the old man closes his *eyes* for him.
Damn. That is *dedication*.
Then a boy wakes up laughing like a lunatic, and that boy is Airen *Farreira*.
Everyone calls him the Lazy Lord, because since his mother died he has done nothing but *sleep*. That's one way to waste a decade.
The guards gush that his little sister Kiril became a royal sorcerer at eleven, so you can guess who gets all the *attention*.
Kiril hears the guards gossip about her brother and tears into them, until her mother, Baroness Amelia, *calms* her down.
But Airen wakes up that night shaking and drenched in sweat, because the dream felt way too *real*.
His hands won't stop trembling, and one word fills his head, *sword*.
He asks his butler for a sword, and the poor man nearly drops *dead*.
So he walks into the training hall, grabs the biggest sword on the wall, and his arms shake like *jelly*.
Every swing is pathetic, and two nobles watching bet he quits in three *days*.
He collapses again and again, but each swing wipes away a little *bitterness*. That was either brave or stupid.
By day four the guards are betting money on whether he shows *up*.
And a hooded old knight in the corner watches him very *closely*.
Then a giant *griffin* drops out of the sky, with Kiril riding it like an Uber.
She is furious. She yells that swordsmanship is no *joke*, and calls him pathetic in front of the whole yard.
Then their mother walks in, says one sentence, and Kiril shuts *up*. Mom energy, undefeated.
That night Kiril marches to his room, but the butler stops her at the *door*.
So she leaves an apology and a little stuffed *doll*.
Next morning he eats breakfast with the whole *family*, for the first time in years.
Meanwhile the old knight watches him train and can't look *away*.
So he rushes to the Baron, out of breath, and says this boy has a *gift*.
The Baron hands Airen a letter to Krono Swordsmanship Academy, the best on the *continent*.
He won't force him, but he gives Airen two days to *decide*.
Ten years in bed, and now a sword academy? Airen clenches his fist and says he's done *lying down*.
Two days later his family walks him to the gate, and Kiril slips him a sword *necklace*.
He steps out alone, calls himself a mere trainee, and walks into the *academy*.
At the gate a red-haired guard reads the letter from Sir Bran Sommerville, and *freezes*.
The recruits whisper about the Lazy Prince, and the red-haired man wonders what Sir Bran *saw* in him.
Four hundred trainees fill the hall, and they all *glare* at Airen.
Then the red-haired guard walks on stage, and he is Ahmed, their *instructor*.
He points out the star of the year, Illia Lindsay, a *genius* from a famous house.
Then Ahmed marches them outside and shouts one word, *run*.
Airen is gasping at the back, but he thinks of the man in his dream, and he *gets up*.
He runs on trembling legs, and the blue-haired noble Lloyd stares in *shock*.
Then Airen keels over, and an instructor *catches* him before he hits the dirt.
The test ranked everyone, and Airen came in dead *last*. Four hundred out of four hundred. Brutal.
From now on one strict schedule, and all weapon training is *banned*.
Most trainees hit the gym once and whine, but Airen shows up *every night*.
And there is Illia Lindsay, squatting a barbell like it's a *pillow*.
Trainees snicker at Airen's push-ups, then a red-haired commoner named Judith *snaps* at Lloyd for staring.
Then Illia walks over, fixes Airen's posture herself, and the whole gym goes *silent*.
Judith corners him and demands to know what Illia *said*.
He says it was just posture tips, and she definitely doesn't *buy* it.
One month later nobody has touched a sword, and Airen hasn't missed a single *day*. It's a full Rocky montage.
Three months later even the instructors admit he's no *lazy prince*.
Then Ahmed announces the mid-term, a brutal obstacle *course*, and the academy head watches the top five.
Everyone goes all out, and Airen drags himself through *every* set.
Judith watches him crawl and wonders how a lazy lord has more *willpower* than her.
Then Ian, the ninety-year-old head sword master, wanders into the *gym*.
He asks one question that makes Ahmed freeze, where is Airen *Farreira*?
Airen has been lifting for over thirty minutes, and Ian tells them to leave him *alone*.
That night Airen lies in bed and wonders why Illia keeps *helping* him.
Then he falls asleep, and the red dream *returns*.
A swordsman rises out of the red fog, and Airen grabs his *cloak*.
He thanks him for everything and whispers that it's time to go *now*.
Then he wakes up, and his body looks nothing like the boy who went to *sleep*. What did that dream give him?
